items.Sentence: Headworks consists of an influent flow meter, a submersible pump station (including backup), and two ¼” step screens, in a two-channel system to allow for redundancy.
After the screens, wastewater flows into a vortex aerated grit chamber with a bypass channel and primary clarifier splitter box.
After the screens, wastewater flows into a vortex aerated grit chamber with a bypass channel and primary clarifier splitter box.
The low salts pond receives flow from the primary clarifier splitter box, tertiary filtration reject, sludge beds return flow and captured stormwater.

When high salt concentrations are detected by an electroconductivity meter in the primary clarifier splitter box, wastewater is redirected as high salt flow to 1 mm rotary drum screens with flows directed to a shotcrete-lined high TDS pond.
Biological and filtered treatment for high salt concentration wastewater is performed by a membrane bioreactor (MBR).
This flow is pumped over the course of the next 24-hour period to a MBR for biological treatment and ultrafiltration (UF).
Filtration of the low salt concentration wastewater stream is performed by the UF membrane facility.
The high salts treatment train flows from the MBR to a reverse osmosis (RO) system for advanced treatment.
Each of the three units houses a cartridge filter assembly and 40 spiral wound medium pressure membranes contained in 8 pressure vessels in a 4:2:1:1 four stage array.
The UV disinfection system disinfects the comingled flows from the background UF permeate (low TDS treatment train) and the RO permeate (high TDS treatment train).
Each aeration basin has six zones and bypassing capabilities with various settings for anaerobic, anoxic, or oxic functions.

Secondary treatment systems for low salts wastewater consists of an aeration basin/mixed liquor splitter box, three aeration basins, two secondary clarifiers, a return activated sludge (RAS) and wasted activated sludge (WAS) pump station, and two equalization ponds.

Solids from the two secondary clarifiers are sent to concrete lined beds for drying and hauled off annually to the Engel & Gray composting facility.
The destination of biosolids produced is Engel & Gray located at 745 Betteravia Road, Santa Maria, California
